The only change in docs/architecture/inference.md is one added table row at head line 1409. It documents `decodeStepsBetweenPrefillChunks`: 4 for the Qwen 3.5 family (`Qwen35Model`, including `Qwen35MoEModel`), 0 otherwise, sourced from `EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift` (`qwenDecodeStepsBetweenPrefillChunks`). It is documentation only; no source, config, wire protocol, key handling, attestation or authorization code changes in the supplied evidence.

The two supplied units are base-side text of the file at lines 2420-2981 (MiMo/Flint/Qwen4 prose, invariants, failure modes, code map). Neither contains the changed line, and I found nothing in them that interacts with the added row. I checked them against the threat model: T-041/TB-007 (prefix cache and SSD tier), T-008 (fail-closed encryption), T-010 (cancellation), T-029 (idle GPU), T-050 (media temp files, which the SDK's in-memory video asset language does not contradict), T-056 and TB-012 (add-on hold). The base text describes existing behavior only; the PR does not change it.

The added setting would interleave decode steps between prefill chunks. It plausibly affects latency and scheduling fairness (availability, T-029/T-010 class), not confidentiality or authorization. The underlying code change is not in this batch, so I cannot verify that the code matches the doc or that the setting preserves cancellation, lease and KV-budget invariants (Invariants 2 and 4). The next review pass should check `EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift` and the scheduler for this. This is an unverified contract, not a finding. No threat-model update is needed from this doc line alone.
